root_cause.text: The mshv_vtl driver fails to clamp the calculated pgmap->vmemmap_shift value to MAX_FOLIO_ORDER, allowing excessively large compound page orders derived from highly aligned physical addresses to be passed to memremap_pages(), which rejects them as unsupported folio sizes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies the calculation of pgmap->vmemmap_shift to use min(count_trailing_zeros(...), MAX_FOLIO_ORDER) instead of just count_trailing_zeros(...), and updates the error path to return PTR_ERR(addr) instead of hard-coding -EFAULT to expose the underlying -EINVAL.

relevance_review.reason: The change only removes an explanatory comment and does not implement the necessary clamping logic for pgmap->vmemmap_shift to MAX_FOLIO_ORDER required to fix the vulnerability.

The change only adds explanatory comments regarding the VTL0 pagemap range end calculation. It does not implement the critical logic fix required to clamp pgmap->vmemmap_shift to MAX_FOLIO_ORDER, which is the direct solution to the vulnerability root cause.

The vulnerability root cause is the failure to clamp `vmemmap_shift` to `MAX_FOLIO_ORDER`, allowing invalid values to reach `memremap_pages`. Group 3 only modifies error propagation logic to preserve specific error codes instead of masking them as `EFAULT`. It does not address the missing validation or clamping logic required to fix the vulnerability.

This group only adds inline documentation about last_pfn exclusion semantics. It does not address the vulnerability root cause, which requires clamping pgmap->vmemmap_shift to MAX_FOLIO_ORDER to prevent excessively large compound page orders from being passed to memremap_pages().

The vulnerable code allowed excessively large compound page orders from highly aligned physical addresses to pass through to memremap_pages() without validation, causing it to reject unsupported folio sizes.
